S55.01.note: The Settings opener was not traced; the earlier running-app check reported a wide directory with 0 indexed connectors.
steps: Sign in and open Settings (the account menu entry that opens Settings was not traced in code).
Click Connectors in the Settings list.
Click Add, then Browse connectors.
Look for a catalogue of connectors, each showing its name, publisher and connection state, and compare with Expected.

S55.02.note: The placeholder found is for the Connectors pane search; the directory toolbar search text was not confirmed.
steps: Open Browse connectors as in S55.01.
Click the search box in the directory and type part of a connector name, a publisher or a tool word.
Watch the list narrow.
Compare the shown entries with Expected.

S55.03.note: The exact visible filter-group label was not found; category filter is built in apps/web/features/directory/services/connectors-directory.ts.
steps: Open Browse connectors as in S55.01.
Open the filter control in the directory toolbar and choose a category such as Productivity or Developer.
Check that only connectors in that category remain.
Compare with Expected.

S55.04.note: Detail page is packages/ui/ui/src/directory/ConnectorDetailView.tsx; exact headings were not confirmed.
steps: Open Browse connectors as in S55.01.
Click a connector card such as GitHub.
Read the detail page: description, publisher, sign-in requirement, tools and links.
Compare with Expected.
S55.04.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > click a connector card (e.g. GitHub)

S55.05.note: The operations list is in packages/ui/ui/src/directory/ConnectorDetailView.tsx; its heading text was not confirmed.
steps: Open a connector's detail page as in S55.04, before connecting.
Scroll to the list of operations or tools.
Compare the list with Expected.
S55.05.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > click a connector card (e.g. GitHub)

S55.06.note: The scope list component is shown; I did not confirm it is rendered before connecting rather than only after.
steps: Open a connector's detail page before connecting.
Read the permissions text, in plain words, on the page.
Compare what can be read and what can be changed with Expected.
S55.06.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > click a connector card (e.g. GitHub)

S55.07.needs: an outside account (Google or GitHub) and a configured connector
S55.07.note: Earlier run recorded this as blocked by deployment configuration (missing GitHub App setup).
steps: Open a connector's detail page as in S55.04.
Click Connect.
Watch whether the real sign-in or authorization flow starts.
Compare with Expected.
S55.07.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > GitHub > Connect

S55.08.needs: an outside account (Google) that can approve access
S55.08.note: Provider consent page and grant storage cannot be seen from the app's own screens; earlier run blocked by external authorization setup.
steps: Open an OAuth connector's detail page, such as Google Drive.
Click Connect.
Check that the provider's consent page opens.
After approving, check that the connector shows as connected.
S55.08.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > an OAuth connector > Connect

S55.09.needs: an API key for a connector that uses one
S55.09.note: Encrypted storage is not visible to the tester; only the form and the result can be checked.
steps: Open a connector that needs an API key.
Click Connect and enter the key in the form.
Click Test and save.
Check that the connector shows as connected, and compare with Expected.
S55.09.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > an API-key connector > Connect

labels.text: What this workspace shares, and the access level of each grant.

S55.11.needs: an organization admin account and a second member account in the same organization
S55.11.note: The route to Workspace > Sharing from the app menu was not traced.
steps: Sign in as an organization admin and open the workspace Sharing page.
Find the connectors section and share a connector with the organization.
Sign in as a second member of the same organization and check the connector can be used without entering its credential.
Compare with Expected.

S55.13.note: Account name logic is in apps/web/lib/connectors/accounts.ts; I did not find the screen text that shows it. Searched the connector settings components and directory for the display.

S55.14.note: Account identity logic is in apps/web/lib/connectors/accounts.ts; no screen text showing email or domain was found in the connector components.

S55.17.needs: a connected connector (a paid or Free account depending on the connector)
S55.17.note: The list renders only when at least one scope exists.
steps: Connect a connector, or open one that is already connected.
Open its detail page.
Read the Permissions granted list.
Compare the listed permissions with Expected.
S55.17.where: Settings > Connectors > (connected connector, e.g. Google Drive) > click the connector card

S55.18.needs: a connector whose grant has expired or been revoked, or a healthy one
S55.18.note: Visible words for healthy and not-responding states were not found; only the reauthorization state was confirmed.
steps: Open Settings > Connectors.
Look at each connector's status label.
Check that a connector needing reauthorization shows Reconnect.
Compare with Expected.

S55.20.needs: a revoked or expired OAuth grant, for example Google Drive
S55.20.note: The plan file marks this as unfinished (partial code), so the tester should expect a gap.
steps: Use a connector whose OAuth grant was revoked or expired.
Open Settings > Connectors and find the Reconnect button beside Disconnect.
Click Reconnect and check that the authorization flow runs again.
Check that connector settings and tool permissions remain, and that a chat shows the reconnect card.
S55.20.where: Settings > Connectors > (connector needing reauthorization, e.g. Google Drive) > Reconnect

S55.21.note: The capabilities panel (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx) has a retry, but no visible on-demand test-connection control text was found.

S55.22.note: The confirmation title is built in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-modal/SettingsModal.tsx.
steps: Open a connected connector's detail page in Settings > Connectors.
Click Disconnect.
Read the confirmation dialog titled Disconnect <name>? and confirm.
Ask the assistant to use the connector and check it is no longer available.

S55.23.needs: a connected connector and the provider account (outside the app)
S55.23.note: No separate Revoke control was found; the provider token revocation runs behind Disconnect.
steps: Disconnect a connected connector as in S55.22.
Check the connector no longer shows as connected.
Check in the provider's own account security page that the app's access is gone.

S55.25.needs: a connector that supports folder or repository limits
S55.25.note: The route apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts and the hook apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx were found, but no visible control for choosing folders or repositories was found in the connector components.

S55.26.note: A Tool permissions label exists and the panel groups tools into Read-only tools and Write and delete tools (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx), but no separate read-only switch was found.

S55.27.note: Allow, Needs approval each time and Never run this tool are the level labels in ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx; the approval action words are defined in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts.
steps: Open a connected connector's detail page.
Click Tool permissions.
For a tool, pick Allow, Needs approval each time, or Never run this tool.
Check that a destructive tool shows Always asks: destructive, and compare with Expected.

S55.28.needs: a Free or paid account, and a connector that is not connected yet
S55.28.note: The summary appears in apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorConsentDialog.tsx; the exact retention sentence was not read in full.
steps: Click Connect on a connector that is not yet connected.
Read the consent dialog before the connection starts.
Check the data retention point in the summary.
Compare with Expected.
S55.28.where: Settings > Connectors > Add > Browse connectors > a connector > Connect (consent step)

S55.29.needs: a connected connector used in a chat
S55.29.note: The chat timeline groups connector tool calls by connector name (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ToolTimeline.tsx), but the provider attribution text was not found. apps/web/features/connectors/lib/mcp-tool-name.ts no longer exists.

S55.30.needs: a connector granted with fewer scopes than the task needs
S55.30.note: The card headline is built from a template string, so the word Reconnect is taken from that file.
steps: Connect a connector with limited access.
In chat, ask for a task that needs more access than granted.
Look for a connector card in the chat with a Reconnect button.
Compare with Expected.
S55.30.where: Chat > ask for a task that needs a connector scope the grant lacks (e.g. read a GitHub issue after granting only part of the access)
